payload.subject: Mathematics
payload.lesson_type_evidence: We can subtract 47 from 72, but we need to borrow some rupees from our neighbour, who has 10 rupees.

concept_map.concept: Making Coin Combinations for a Given Amount

learning_objectives: Students will be able to subtract two-digit numbers using borrowing/regrouping.
Students will apply mental math strategies (doubles, near doubles) for quick addition and subtraction.
Students will understand the concept of subtracting zero and subtracting a number from itself.
Students will be able to make different combinations of coins to make a given amount.
learning_outcomes: Students can solve subtraction problems involving borrowing with accuracy.
Students use doubles and near doubles to compute sums and differences mentally.
Students explain why subtracting zero leaves a number unchanged and why subtracting a number from itself yields zero.
Students represent a given amount using various coin combinations and verify the total.
prerequisites: Understanding of place value (tens and ones)
misconceptions: Students may forget to borrow from the tens place when needed.
Students may borrow from the wrong place value.
Students may subtract the smaller digit from the larger digit in each column without considering the need to borrow.
Students may think borrowing changes the value of the number incorrectly.
suggested_instructional_sequence: Review place value and simple subtraction without borrowing.
Introduce borrowing concept using concrete manipulatives (e.g., base-ten blocks).
Demonstrate borrowing with two-digit numbers through guided examples.
Provide practice problems for subtraction with borrowing.
Introduce mental math strategies: doubles and near doubles.
Explore subtracting zero and subtracting a number from itself with real-life examples.
Apply learning to money problems: making different coin combinations for a given amount.
Review and assess understanding through varied exercises.
